title: Elementary submodels: Tarski–Vaught and Löwenheim–Skolem
summary: Find smaller structures that agree on every first-order formula with parameters, using the witness criterion and downward Löwenheim–Skolem.
abstract: The positive natural numbers inherit their order from the natural numbers, yet removing zero changes whether one has a smaller element. A smaller domain can lose witnesses to existential statements. An elementary submodel preserves the truth of every first-order formula whose parameters lie in that domain. The Tarski–Vaught criterion says that it is enough to keep a witness whenever an existential statement has one in the larger structure. Repeatedly adjoining chosen witnesses produces a countable elementary submodel in any countable language, even inside an uncountable structure, and the same construction gives a cardinal bound for larger languages and prescribed sets of parameters.
